headline: NAB's Group CET1 ratio (APRA Level 2) fell 65 bps over FY25, from 12.35% at 30 Sep 2024 to 11.70% at 30 Sep 2025 - the results-book KPI figure and the bank's headline capital measure, comfortably above its >11.25% operating target. The only driver NAB quantifies in bps for the full year is the buy-back: $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25, -15 bps. Its FY narrative also names lending volume growth and increased long-term investment in the business, without bps. Neither document publishes a full-year capital walk: the only walk (results book and presentation) runs Mar 25 to Sep 25 and is context only - 2H25 bars: cash earnings +82, dividend -61, credit RWA -45, other RWA +1, other -8. Over the FY window the capital table shows credit RWA up 6.9% ($350,891m to $374,986m), total RWA up 6.4% to $440,557m, and the capital floor moving from nil to $2,284m. Residual: -50 bps of the stated -65 bps is not attributed in FY bps. Pro forma 11.81% includes the post-balance-date MLC Life sale; internationally comparable CET1 of 17.1% (Sep 25) is a different measure.

drivers.narrative: The only FY-window bps the bank prints: '$0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25 (-15 bps)'. The $3.0 billion on-market buy-back completed 12 March 2025; 16,572,039 shares bought back in FY25, 0.15% of CET1 capital (87.8 million shares in total).

FY window: credit RWA +6.9% ($350,891m to $374,986m), total RWA +6.4% to $440,557m. Bank names 'lending volume growth'. Mar-Sep 25 ONLY: credit RWA -45 bps (volume -27, asset quality -5, models -13); higher CRWA from business lending growth and overlays; NPE +$1,864m or 18.2% to $12,094m.

drivers.bank_label: Models and methodology changes (within credit RWA)
drivers.narrative: Mar-Sep 25 ONLY: model and methodology changes -13 bps, including a $4.8bn RWA overlay on the measurement of certain off-balance-sheet exposures. No FY-window bps disclosed. APRA's APS 117 IRRBB revisions took effect 1 October 2025, after balance date, so no FY25 impact.

Floor adjustment RWA: nil at 30 Sep 24, $1,256m at 31 Mar 25, $2,284m at 30 Sep 25. Mar-Sep 25 ONLY: -3 bps. The internationally comparable measure excludes the impact of the Basel capital floor. No FY-window bps disclosed.
Mar-Sep 25 ONLY: cash earnings +82 bps, and +21 bps net of the 2025 interim dividend. No FY-window earnings bps are disclosed, so the full-year earnings contribution is left unquantified.
Mar-Sep 25 ONLY: dividend bar -61 bps. No FY-window dividend or DRP bps are disclosed; the bank does not quantify dividends net of DRP for the full year in the documents cited.

drivers.bank_label: Other (net FX translation, non-cash earnings, software, reserves)
drivers.narrative: Mar-Sep 25 ONLY: other items -8 bps, including net foreign exchange translation, non-cash earnings, capitalised software and other miscellaneous items. No FY-window bps disclosed for this bucket.

Sale of the Group's remaining 20% stake in MLC Life for $497m completed 31 October 2025 - after the balance date. It lifts the pro forma ratio to 11.81% and contributes nothing to the FY25 reported movement.

notable_items: FY25 buy-back impact of -15 bps from $0.6bn of shares bought back (0.15% of CET1 capital)
CET1 operating target raised by 25 bps to >11.25% in May 2025 following APRA's AT1 phase-out decision
Pro forma CET1 ratio of 11.81% reflects the post-balance-date (31 Oct 2025) sale of the remaining 20% of MLC Life for $497m

disagreements.topic: APRA Level 2 CET1 vs internationally comparable CET1 (Sep 25)
disagreements.explanation: NAB's headline capital measure is the APRA Level 2 Group CET1 ratio. The internationally comparable ratio is a different measure excluding the Basel capital floor and other APRA-specific requirements; it is context, never the movement.

limitations: No full-year CET1 walk is published in either document; the only walks cover Mar 25 to Sep 25 (the prior half) and are treated as context. Their bars (+82 cash earnings, -61 dividend, -45 credit RWA, +1 other RWA, -8 other) were NOT restated as FY contributions.
Only -15 bps of the stated -65 bps movement is quantified by the bank for the FY window (buy-back); the residual -50 bps is unattributed in FY bps.

The bank's FY narrative names lending volume growth and increased long-term investment as reduction drivers without bps; all sub-driver bps figures (volume -27, asset quality -5, models -13, floor -3, other -8, cash earnings +82, dividend -61) belong to Mar-Sep 25 only and were not restated as FY contributions.

RWA evidence is FY-level totals only (credit +6.9% to $374,986m; total +6.4% to $440,557m; floor nil to $2,284m); no FY bps decomposition of credit RWA, and no FY bps for the floor, dividends, FX or other items.

The results book's capital table also prints market risk, operational risk and IRRBB RWA rows, and the presentation prints Level 1 CET1 figures (p7) and the Sep 24 internationally comparable CET1 ratio (p106); these could not be captured as evidence records before budget exhaustion and are therefore not attributed or quantified here.

The CET1 row in the capital ratios table carries no basis label; it is NAB's APRA Level 2 Group regulatory ratio, reported under the bank's primary framing per the KPI page, and 'cash' basis is recorded per the unlabelled-row convention.

Plan items 'Level 1 and internationally comparable ratio rows as context' and 'RWA movement detail (market/operational/IRRBB)' are only partially closed for this reason; the Sep 25 internationally comparable CET1 ratio of 17.1% is evidenced via the p106 reconciliation walk (ev-9).
Research stopped early: the wall-clock budget (1800s) was reached, so the evidence behind this answer is less complete than a full run's.
No published walk covers FY25 vs FY24: the bank's walk for this metric describes another comparison, so the driver split is not walk-verified for this comparison. Confidence is capped at 85.
